deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous pages): X is a set, later a topological space, and Λ is a coefficient ring. Grothendieck studies families F of subsets of X satisfying axioms a)–f), together with the associated algebra A_F of Λ-valued functions. For a finite partition P = (X_i)_{i∈I} of X, F_P is the Boolean algebra of unions of the X_i, and A_{F_P} is the algebra of functions constant on each X_i. On the previous page he showed that, for a topological space X, axiom c) is equivalent to (1°): each closure X̄_i is a union of strata, i.e. the frontier condition. He then introduced (2°): X̄_i = X̄_j ⇒ i = j.

This page proves that (1°)+(2°) imply that every X_i is locally closed.
- Define on I the incidence relation i ≺ j ⇔ X̄_i ⊂ X̄_j. It is a preorder, and by (2°) a partial order.
- Take a minimal stratum X_{i0}. By (1°), X̄_{i0} − X_{i0} is a union of strata X_j with j ≠ i0. Each such j satisfies X̄_j ⊂ X̄_{i0}, i.e. j ≺ i0 strictly, which contradicts minimality. So X̄_{i0} − X_{i0} = ∅: a minimal stratum is closed.
- Induct on the number of strata. Replace X by the open set X − X_{i0} with the induced partition. Closures in an open subspace are traces of closures, so (1°) and (2°) persist. Hence every stratum is closed in an open set, i.e. locally closed.
- Consequently F_P is generated (as a Boolean algebra) by closed members, and axiom d) holds automatically.

Definitions. He calls a finite partition satisfying 1) and 2) an 'admissible (finite) stratification' of X. It is 'strict' if moreover 3) every X_i is connected.

Claim. Given 1) and 2), condition 3) is equivalent to axiom f) for F_P: every locally closed A ∈ F_P has finitely many connected components, all lying in F_P. One direction is begun here: X_i is locally closed, lies in F_P, and is a minimal nonempty element of F_P, so its components (which lie in F_P) force X_i to be connected. The converse is on the next page.

Margin note: the frontier condition in the form 'if X_i meets X̄_j then X_i ⊂ X̄_j', i.e. incidence implies containment.

The next page passes to the quotient Y = X/R ≅ I, a finite topological space. In modern terms: (1°)+(2°) say exactly that X → X/R is a continuous map to a finite T0 (Alexandrov) space, whose specialization order is the incidence order. This is the 'poset-stratified space' viewpoint. The whole serves the axiomatics of 'tame' (modérée) constructible sets and functions underlying the tame-topology programme.
errors: Minor: the final line reads 'd) ⇒ 3)', but the argument given (X_i locally closed, in F_P, with components in F_P) uses axiom f). Logically it should be 'f) ⇒ 3)'; probably a slip, or d) refers to a version of the axiom I cannot see.

The inductive step tacitly uses that the induced partition on the open set X − X_{i0} still satisfies 1) and 2). This is true because closure in an open subspace equals the trace of the closure, but it is not stated.
The argument is otherwise correct. Condition 2) is genuinely necessary: two points in an indiscrete space satisfy 1) but the strata are not locally closed.

ideas.what: For a finite partition, 'frontier condition + distinct closures' is equivalent to 'strata locally closed + frontier condition'. Proved by showing minimal strata (for the closure order) are closed, then inducting.
ideas.modern_name: Finite stratification satisfying the frontier condition; locally closed strata
ideas.where_published: Constructible sets and stratifications appear in EGA IV/SGA 4; this exact lemma, unsure

ideas.what: Incidence order on strata, i ≺ j iff X̄_i ⊂ X̄_j, made a partial order by 2); the quotient X/R is a finite topological space indexed by I.
ideas.modern_name: Poset-stratified space: continuous map to a finite T0/Alexandrov space with specialization order
ideas.usually_credited_to: Alexandrov (1937) for finite spaces; MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie (Higher Algebra App. A, 2017), Ayala–Francis–Tanaka for the stratification formulation
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 discusses tame stratified spaces but not, to my knowledge, this explicit finite-space formulation

ideas.what: 'Strict' admissible stratification (connected strata), characterized via the Boolean algebra F_P: locally closed members have finitely many connected components, all in F_P (axiom f).
ideas.modern_name: Connected (irreducible-type) strata; definable/o-minimal cell-decomposition-style axioms for constructible sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (1980s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) sketches tame topology axiomatics in spirit only

missed.claim: In 1974 Grothendieck treats a finite stratification satisfying the frontier condition as a partition whose quotient is a finite ordered space (incidence order). This is essentially the 'stratification = continuous map to a finite poset with Alexandrov topology' definition now standard in higher-categorical stratified homotopy theory. It also ties this to an axiomatic Boolean algebra of 'tame' sets and Λ-valued functions.
missed.quote: Considérons la relation dans I  i ≺ j ⇔ X̄_i ⊂ X̄_j (relation d'incidence des feuilles). C'est une relation de préordre, et grâce à 2) une relation d'ordre.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is an early archival instance of the poset-stratification viewpoint, embedded in an axiomatic tame-topology framework that predates o-minimality. This is of historical rather than technical interest, since the lemmas are elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is elementary point-set topology: minimal strata are closed, induction gives local closedness, and connected strata are characterized. The only mildly notable aspect is the early (1974) framing of stratifications via the incidence order and finite quotient space within a tame-topology axiomatics, which anticipates later poset-stratified formalisms.
